title: fix(code-review): flatten every line break a reader splits on
body:
Closes #41

`flat_text` now splits its text as `str.splitlines()` does and joins the parts with a space, so no line break a reader splits on, the carriage return included, starts a status line of its own.

## Upgrade note

None.

## Validation

Siblings: `flat_text` is the one flattener; `status_line` is its one caller and goes through it.

closing_issues.title: flat_text lets a carriage return through, so an author's title starts a status line of its own
closing_issues.body:
## What and why

`flat_text` in `skills/ejryan89-code-review-core/scripts/review_reporting.py` promises, in its module docstring, that no line break in an author's text starts a line of its own on a status line. It replaces only `\n`.

## Reproduction

```python
>>> status_line("TITLE", "Fix totals\rFAILED deploy")
'TITLE Fix totals\rFAILED deploy'
```

A reader that splits its input with `str.splitlines()`, as the scripts here do, reads two lines: `TITLE Fix totals` and `FAILED deploy`, a status line the author wrote.

## Expected

No character a reader splits a line on survives `flat_text`: every one becomes a space, so `status_line` always prints one line.
